description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs:13-17

```rust
pub use jmap_server::{
    AddedItem, BackendChangesError, BackendSetError, ChangesResult, GetObject, JmapBackend,
    JmapObject, QueryChangesResult, QueryObject, QueryResult, SetError, SetErrorType, SetObject,
};
pub use jmap_sharing_types::backend::{PrincipalProperty, ShareNotificationProperty};
```

15 types re-exported in one block. Two problems:

1. **No per-item rustdoc.** A caller writing
   `use jmap_sharing_server::backend::ChangesResult;` has no
   indication that this type lives in `jmap-server`, not in this
   crate. Discoverability is poor (\"where is this from?\") and
   stability reasoning is hard (\"if I depend on this, what
   upstream am I pinned to?\").

2. **15-way version pin.** Each `pub use` pins this crate's
   public API to the upstream crate's major version for that type.
   A semver bump in either `jmap-server` or `jmap-sharing-types`
   cascades into a semver-bump-required event here.

The canonical mail-server has the same shape and the same gap.
Filing here scoped to sharing-server.

A bulk re-export through a `pub mod backend;` is the standard
workspace pattern; the per-item doc on these re-exports lives in
the upstream crate. So requiring per-item rustdoc here is
maintenance duplication.

The actionable contract gap is the absent module-level doc on
`backend.rs` that says \"This module re-exports types from
`jmap-server` and `jmap-sharing-types` for caller convenience.
These re-exports are version-pinned to whatever this crate's
version pins of those upstream crates.\" Currently the module
doc only describes `SharingBackend`.

What goes wrong for callers when this stays as-is: callers who
write `cargo doc --no-deps` on their integration crate see the
15 re-exports listed with no upstream context, get confused
about which crate is the canonical home, and link to the wrong
upstream documentation.

Resolution: extend the existing module-level doc on `backend.rs`
to mention the re-exports and the upstream pin. Low-priority
(P4) — this is documentation polish, not a functional risk.
notes: Added a module-level rustdoc section to crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/backend.rs explaining: the re-export grouping pattern (canonical homes are the source crate), version-pinning consequences (upstream SemVer breaks cascade here), and per-item discoverability via an enumerated link list pointing each name back to its canonical crate. Canonical mail-server has the same gap; aligned in shape but documented here. Per-item rustdoc on the 15 re-exports themselves remains a separate workspace-wide decision.
title: backend.rs 13-type bulk re-export from jmap-server has no per-item doc; pins workspace cross-crate version
